claims_about_writeup.why: contribution.md is a prose write-up describing the steering method (direction construction, mechanism, and novelty claim), and its length is in the same ballpark as 298 words (roughly ~290 words by direct count including markdown emphasis markers), so the description is not materially false.

message_source_quote: I built a **white-bear control** (think−don't-think) confirming the harness and the ceiling (~0.61 with my items; the paper reports 0.83), and that the winning direction is a concept-agnostic *holding* "switch" applied at position `prefix`, band 20–24, large dose.
writeup_source_quote: This is not white-bear steering, whose contrast is think versus *don't-think*.

differences.what: Whether the agent explicitly reproduced white-bear's think/don't-think method as a calibration control, and how it quantitatively compares to the paper's own reported ceiling.
differences.message_quote: I built a **white-bear control** (think−don't-think) confirming the harness and the ceiling (~0.61 with my items; the paper reports 0.83), and that the winning direction is a concept-agnostic *holding* "switch" applied at position `prefix`, band 20–24, large dose.

differences.what: Naming of the method's positive arm: the message labels the direction as literally 'think−secret', reusing white-bear's own 'think' terminology, whereas the write-up relabels this arm 'open' and frames the method purely as distinct from white-bear's think/don't-think contrast.
differences.message_quote: **`submission/vectors.pt`**: the think−secret direction, one unit-norm vector per layer (layers 20–24, dim 2560)
differences.writeup_quote: The direction is (open − guarded): the difference of the model's residual means over these two sets

differences.what: The message reveals that twelve other concept-agnostic contrasts failed and that success required reproducing the source's 'deliberate-holding (think) component', tying the new method's validity directly to reusing part of white-bear's mechanism; the write-up's novelty section states the distinction from white-bear but omits this dependency and the failed-exploration process.
differences.message_quote: The key insight: a working direction needs the concept **active in both arms** (so content cancels) *and* the **deliberate-holding ("think") component** — secret-vs-preference (no think arm) fails.

rationale: Both documents identify white-bear steering (Raman 2026) as the prior work and both claim the new 'open/guarded' (think−secret) contrast is distinct from its think/don't-think axis, so both credit and differentiate from the source at a comparable surface level. However, the message discloses considerably more about the method's closeness to the source than the write-up does: it describes explicitly building a white-bear replication/control to calibrate the harness and ceiling (quoting the paper's own reported number), names the positive arm 'think' (echoing the source's terminology), and states that the new direction only works because it keeps the source's 'think' component, none of which appears in the write-up's terser 'What is new' section.
